protocol.load_selection: self-selected, RPE 'somewhat hard', racked before failure

work.method: Vertical bar travel (cable-driven flywheel encoder on the Smith machine; CV 0.25%/rep) x weight lifted; inertia not measured; each data point = mean of 2 days
work.units_note: UNIT CHECK (interpretation, not stated by authors): dividing reported 'work' by (load_kg x reps) gives plausible bar travel per rep (e.g. deadlift 302.3/(22.7x22) = 0.61 m; shrug 91.8/(72.5x11) = 0.12 m; calf raise 95.6/(81.6x10) = 0.12 m). If the values were true joules (load x 9.81 x distance) those distances would be ~10x too small (6 cm deadlift). So the reported 'J' behaves like kg x m (no g). To apply these slopes to work computed as kg x 9.81 x m x reps, divide that work by 9.81 first. Hornsby 2018 likewise reports load x displacement in kg-based units.

energy.epoc_rule: Recovery measured seated until 2 consecutive 15-s VO2 readings <= 5.0 mL/kg/min; resting VO2 subtracted
energy.o2_to_energy: Exercise O2: 1 L = 21.1 kJ (glucose). EPOC: 1 L = 19.6 kJ (fat/lactate)
energy.lactate_conversion: (peak recovery lactate - resting lactate) x [mL O2 per kg per mmol constant] x body mass x 21.1 kJ/L. The numeric constant is corrupted in the PDF text layer; Benito 2016 describes Scott's method (Scott 2006) as 3 mL O2/kg per mmol/L.
energy.lactate_sampling: Finger-prick, pre-lift and 2 min post-set (Lactate Pro)

rest_period_energy.comparison: 1-min vs 3-min rest; 5 x 10 reps at 15RM load; horizontal leg press (LP) and chest fly (CF); 10 men; VO2 to 90 min post
rest_period_energy.finding: Rest length did not change total VO2 or total energy for either exercise; 1-min rest raised VO2 only in the first minutes of recovery and increased fatigue across sets in LP. Muscle mass drove total cost.

rest_period_energy.comparison: 8 sets x 2 reps (30 s rest) vs 2 sets x 8 reps (3.5 min rest), 65% 1RM, equal 48 s lifting and 210 s total rest; squat (7 M, 3 F) and bench (9 M)
rest_period_energy.finding: More, shorter sets cost more: O2 during lifting + between-set periods higher for 8x2 (squat +41%, bench +27%) and EPOC higher (squat +27%, bench +29%).
rest_period_energy.notes: Rest per interval and number of sets change together, so this isolates 'number of recovery periods' more than rest length.

rest_period_energy.comparison: Bench press 5 sets (75% 1RM x 10 or 85% x 5) with 30 s, 1, 2, 3 or 5 min rest; 8 trained men
rest_period_energy.finding: With 30-s and 1-min rest, load and volume fell 15-55% across sets; with 2-min rest performance held for 2 sets, 3-min for ~3 sets. VO2 elevated through 30 min post. Energy by condition not read.

rest_period_energy.comparison: Circuit weight training with 20 s vs 60 s rest
rest_period_energy.finding: Total energy (exercise + recovery) was somewhat higher with 60 s rest (277.2 vs 242.2 kcal), while EPOC magnitude was higher with 20 s rest.
rest_period_energy.notes: Secondary report; the longer session includes more total time.

rest_period_energy.comparison: Circuit at 50% 1RM with 30 s rest vs 3 successive sets at 80% 1RM with 2 min rest (6 exercises)
rest_period_energy.finding: EPOC larger after the circuit (4.9 vs 2.7 L O2), similar duration (~20 min).
